source_text: Καὶ οὐδὲν ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, οὐχ αἵρεσις, οὐ γνώμη ἑτέρα καὶ ἑτέρα, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ μόνον ἄνθρωποι ἐκαλοῦντο, ἑνὸς χείλους καὶ μιᾶς γλώττης. Ἦν δὲ μόνον ἀσέβεια καὶ εὐσέβεια ὁ κατὰ φύσιν νόμος, καὶ ἡ κατὰ φύσιν ἑνὸς ἑκάστου προαίρεσις τοῦ θελήματος, καὶ οὐκ ἀπὸ διδασκαλίας, οὔτε ἀπὸ συγγραμμάτων συγγραφέων πλάνη· οὐκ Ἰουδαϊσμός, οὐχ αἵρεσίς τις ἑτέρα, ἀλλ᾽, ὡς εἰπεῖν, ἡ νῦν πίστις ἐμπολιτευομένη τῇ ἄρτι ἁγίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καθολικῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς οὖσα, καὶ ὕστερον πάλιν ἀποκαλυφθεῖσα. Τῷ γὰρ βουλομένῳ φιλαλήθως ἰδεῖν ἀρχὴ πάντων ἐστὶν ἡ καθολικὴ καὶ ἁγία Ἐκκλησία ἐξ αὐτοῦ τοῦ σκοποῦ. Ἀδὰμ γὰρ πρωτόπλαστος πέπλασται, οὐκ ἐμπερίτομος, ἀλλ᾽ ἀκροβύστης μὲν τῇ σαρκί· οὐκ εἰδωλολάτρης δέ· ᾔδει Πατέρα Θεόν, καὶ Υἱόν, καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα· προφήτης γὰρ ἦν. Οὐκ ἔχων τοίνυν περιτομήν, οὐκ ἦν Ἰουδαῖος· ξόανα δὲ μὴ προσκυνῶν ἢ ἄλλο τι, οὐκ ἦν εἰδωλολάτρης. Προφήτης γὰρ ὁ Ἀδάμ, καὶ ᾔδει ὅτι ὁ Πατὴρ εἶπε τῷ Υἱῷ· Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον. Τί οὖν ἦν μήτε περιτομὴν ἔχων, μήτε εἴδωλα σέβων, ἀλλὰ τοῦ Χριστιανισμοῦ τὸν χαρακτῆρα ὑποφαίνων; οὕτω καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἄβελ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Σήθ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἐνώς, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἐνώχ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Μαθουσάλα, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Νῶε, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἕβερ, ἄχρι τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ διαληπτέον.
thought_title: The original faith before heresy, Judaism, and idolatry
orientation: Epiphanius is opening his treatise by describing the earliest state of humanity, before any heresy or Judaism existed, and arguing that the faith of the catholic and holy Church was present from the beginning.
pass_a_gloss: And there was nothing on the earth, no heresy, no one opinion and another, but only they were called human beings, of one lip and one tongue. And there was only impiety and piety, the natural law, and the natural choice of each one's will, and not from teaching, nor from writings of writers was there error; no Judaism, no other heresy, but, so to speak, the faith now living as a citizen in the just now holy catholic Church of God, being from the beginning, and later again revealed. For to the one willing to see in a truth-loving way, the beginning of all things is the catholic and holy Church from this very point. For Adam the first-formed was formed, not circumcised, but uncircumcised in the flesh; and not an idolater; he knew Father God, and Son, and Holy Spirit; for he was a prophet. Therefore not having circumcision, he was not a Jew; and not worshipping carved images or anything else, he was not an idolater. For Adam was a prophet, and he knew that the Father said to the Son: Let us make a human being. What then was he, neither having circumcision, nor worshipping idols, but showing forth the mark of Christianity? So also in the case of Abel, and in the case of Seth, and in the case of Enosh, and in the case of Enoch, and in the case of Methuselah, and in the case of Noah, and in the case of Eber, one must discuss up to Abraham.

choices.english: of one lip and one tongue
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the bodily metaphor for shared speech, matching the source's concrete terms.
rejected: of one language and one speech
of one mouth and one tongue

choices.why: The verb's political sense (being a citizen) is retained literally rather than flattened to 'existing in.'
The adverb 'just now' is kept to preserve the temporal nuance that the Church is holy at the present time.
The compound is rendered literally to preserve the adverbial force of loving truth.
The verb 'showing forth' and noun 'mark' are kept literal to preserve the image of a visible imprint.
The verbal adjective's impersonal necessity is rendered literally.

pass_b_english: And there was nothing on the earth—no heresy, no one opinion and then another. People were simply called human beings, of one lip and one tongue. There was only impiety and piety, the natural law, and each person's natural choice of the will—not error from teaching or from the writings of authors. There was no Judaism, no other heresy, but, so to speak, the faith that now lives as a citizen in the catholic and holy Church of God existed from the beginning and was later revealed again. For anyone willing to see in a truth-loving way, the catholic and holy Church is the beginning of all things, from this very aim. For Adam was formed as the first-formed man, not circumcised but uncircumcised in the flesh, and not an idolater. He knew God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit—for he was a prophet. Since he did not have circumcision, he was not a Jew; and since he did not worship carved images or anything else, he was not an idolater. For Adam was a prophet, and he knew that the Father said to the Son, "Let us make man" (Genesis 1:26). What then was he, having neither circumcision nor worship of idols, but showing forth the mark of Christianity? So also one must discuss Abel, and Seth, and Enosh, and Enoch, and Methuselah, and Noah, and Eber, up to Abraham.

problems.source_quote: τῇ ἄρτι ἁγίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καθολικῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ
problems.why: "ἄρτι" modifies the whole phrase: "the catholic Church which is now/holy catholic Church of God now"; "just now holy" makes it sound newly holy.
problems.fix: the faith that now lives as a citizen in the holy catholic Church of God

edits.old: the faith that now lives as a citizen in the holy catholic Church of God, which is just now holy, existed from the beginning
edits.new: the faith that now lives as a citizen in the holy catholic Church of God existed from the beginning

fixed: Removed 'which is just now holy' because 'ἄρτι' modifies the whole phrase 'the holy catholic Church of God,' not 'holy' alone; the English now reads 'the faith that now lives as a citizen in the holy catholic Church of God existed from the beginning.'

problems.why: σκοπός means 'aim, goal, viewpoint' not 'point' in a temporal sense; 'from this very aim/goal' or 'from this very perspective'.
problems.ruling: ἐξ αὐτοῦ τοῦ σκοποῦ means 'from this very aim/purpose'; 'point' risks misleading reader into temporal or vague sense.

problems.why: Glossary fixes 'catholic and holy Church' as the order; English inverts to 'holy catholic Church'.
problems.fix: the catholic and holy Church of God

edits.old: the faith that now lives as a citizen in the holy catholic Church of God existed from the beginning
edits.new: the faith that now lives as a citizen in the catholic and holy Church of God existed from the beginning

fixed: The glossary order 'catholic and holy Church' is now applied to the English phrase 'holy catholic Church of God'.

refereed.why: σκοποῦ means 'viewpoint, perspective, consideration' not 'aim'; 'from this very aim' changes the epistemological sense.
refereed.ruling: σκοποῦ means viewpoint/perspective; 'aim' changes epistemological sense from viewing standpoint to goal.

refereed.quote: showing forth the mark of Christianity
refereed.why: ὑποφαίνων means 'showing dimly, hinting at, giving a glimpse of' not 'showing forth'; English overstates the clarity of the revelation.
refereed.fix: giving a glimpse of the mark of Christianity
refereed.ruling: ὑποφαίνων means show dimly/hint at; 'showing forth' overstates clarity, changing meaning.
